S01 has a real narrow-screen advantage: outputs/S01/stable/390-initial-conversation.png shows all three source cards at once, whereas S06 initially shows a cropped rail. Both communicate pending/error states clearly; the preference is modest and does not imply a functional advantage.

The simpler single-column sheet in outputs/S07/stable/390-expanded.png makes more of the source summary visible above its note dock than outputs/S02/stable/390-expanded.png, whose fixed source/control stack is taller. The inspected S07 expansion/reversal originals also retain readable content without the sideways rail cropping seen in outputs/S02/temporal/007-expand-0.png and outputs/S02/temporal/012-reverse-0.png. S02's expanded desktop contents and note rail is a useful counterstrength in outputs/S02/stable/1440-expanded.png. outputs/S10/stable/1440-initial-schedule.png and outputs/S10/stable/900-initial-schedule.png provide a shared calendar scale for comparing project intervals, while S09's date-led agenda in outputs/S09/stable/1440-initial-schedule.png gives less comparative spatial context and shows fewer rows. outputs/S03/stable/1440-initial-detail.png and outputs/S03/stable/900-initial-detail.png fit the inquiry, existing note, note editor, and Save action together with the metadata rail. In outputs/S05/stable/1440-initial-detail.png and outputs/S05/stable/900-initial-detail.png the note field only starts near the bottom, with its continuation beyond the visible footer boundary. S03's compact mobile register shows more working records in outputs/S03/stable/390-initial-projects.png and its compass/ring/dossier language is consistently carried through populated work. overall_limitations: Independent model visual judgments, made in the supplied R1 pair and output order while version-blinded. No source, participant handovers, implementation logs, identity map, other reviewer files, or external research were used.

Actually inspected 333 unique images: all 192 stable originals, all 36 supplied supplemental originals, 78 selected temporal originals, 12 stable overviews, 12 temporal overviews, and three benchmark author images. Overviews were used for orientation; consequential text and detail observations use original-resolution images.

No sequence.webm was watched and no natural continuous playback was observed. Ordered samples establish their captured appearance and order only. Motion smoothness, easing, responsiveness, frame delivery, real elapsed interaction duration, and physical-device gesture quality remain unassessed.

No live interaction was performed. Visible action labels, retained drafts, saved messages, and selected states are evidence of presentation, not independent verification of persistence, source isolation, keyboard behavior, focus trapping, attachment handling, filter correctness, stop/retry results, or backend capabilities.

Only the captured viewport and scroll positions are observable. Content below a fixed note area, composer, or viewport may be scrollable; these reviews do not equate first-screen omission with inaccessible or missing content. The twelve complete project records and every full article were not individually visible.

T1 and T2 have initial and alternate themes at 390, 900, and 1440 pixels. T3 supplies one theme at those widths. No claims cover unprovided viewport sizes, OS text scaling, alternate input modes, color-calibrated displays, or measured accessibility compliance.

The supplied benchmark images inform T1 visual maturity and organization only. Their different content and product scope do not establish a feature-parity requirement. T3 identity judgments concern the sheet's visible relationship to the supplied notebook, not implementation-level preservation.

Scores remain six separate ordinal judgments. Paired preferences express this reviewer's comparative reading of the visible evidence; they are not human-user findings and have not been converted into totals or percentages.
